quoted_phrases: You’ve probably heard of [Loomio](https://www.loomio.org/), the simple but effective decision making software from [Enspiral](https://enspiral.com/), but what you might not have heard about are the patterns and principles which the founders of Loomio use in their own organisation.

It’s not that his patterns for working in groups are entirely novel – it’s that he’s thought about it, and clearly lived by the rules he so passionately espouses, I could almost feel his hard-earned acumen making its way from his brain into my own.

Take the first pattern for example: **“Intentionally produce counter-culture”** which you probably instinctively know is a good idea but what really struck me were the magic words: **“belonging is a superpower”**.
This is something we so often fail to deliver on… If everyone in your group feels the same empowering sense of belonging there’s no limit to what can be achieved.

With pattern 2, **“Systematically distribute care labour”**, Rich talked about everyone in their organisation being a steward for someone else and a stewardee too – to ensure everyone receives adequate support.

Pattern 3 introduced the idea that groups should **“Make explicit norms and boundaries”** in order to avoid any ambiguity about what a group is, how it works, what it finds acceptable and what it will not tolerate.
Pattern 4 addressed the inevitable challenge with the wise words **“Keep talking about power”**.

Pattern 5 **“Make decisions asynchronously”** is so simple it’s surprising that more groups don’t follow the rule: Meetings are great for bonding and building trust, computers are great for helping us make better decisions – which can be more inclusive and less invasive; timely but not hurried.
Pattern 6 addresses the elephant which lurks in every room by asking groups to **“Agree how you use tech”**.

I’ve never seen it put so simply before and this was a little revelation to me; the vast proportion of tech tools can be split into what Rich refers to as the ‘holy trinity’ for group management: A tool for realtime communication (i.e.
Pattern 7 proposed **“Using rhythm to cut information overload”** by providing clear and well planned times for team members to tell others what they are up to and to find out who needs support.

by using quarterly reviews to get everyone out of the office and bonding again (by creating ‘peak oxytocin’ moments!) and shorter cycles for discussing more day-to-day, week-to-week plans, reviews and celebrations.
Pattern 8 encapsulates the overall ethos, that groups should **“Generate new patterns together”**.

![](http://198.38.77.184/~open/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/belonging-superpower-280x300.jpg) Click for a bigger version For the rest of the workshop they split us out into groups in which we defined a challenge we were facing, worked out a “desired future” and “next steps” to get there together.
Our group chose to focus on the process of “on-boarding” and the challenge of empowering everyone, especially newcomers to a group, with the “superpower of belonging”.
The ideas we came up with were many and varied and largely inspired by the patterns above and others’ lived experiences.
You can see the ideas in the “Next steps” section of our worksheet – hopefully some of them will be useful for you in your groups.
I’d like to send a huge THANK YOU out to Rich and Nati for making this event happen and for delivering such a well planned and designed workshop with such timely content.

semantic_findings.answer: jargon clumps where the writer knows things

answer.phrase: I could almost feel his hard-earned acumen making its way from his brain into my own
answer.why_forced: Maps an abstract, non-physical quality (acumen, i.e. accumulated skill/judgment) onto a tactile sensation of feeling and physical transit from one brain to another, with no concrete sensory anchor grounding the claim.

answer.phrase: like a beam of brilliance from above
answer.why_generic: A stock inspirational image (light from above) that could describe any admired speaker; it names no concrete quality of Rich and Nati's actual delivery.

answer.phrase: the elephant which lurks in every room
answer.why_generic: A well-worn cliché for an avoided issue; it substitutes a familiar idiom for any concrete description of what makes tech-tool disagreements awkward in this context.

answer.phrase: which can be more inclusive and less invasive; timely but not hurried
answer.why_formulaic: A stacked pair of balanced antitheses that sounds conclusive but never specifies what makes async decisions inclusive versus invasive, or timely versus hurried, in this particular group's practice.

answer.phrase: The more effective we can make decentralised teams the more positive change we will be able to deliver.
answer.what_it_repeats: Restates the effectiveness claims already made piecemeal after several patterns (e.g. the steward system being 'bound to reduce conflicts' and tech-tool agreement making a team 'bound to be more effective') without adding new information.

answer.missing_criterion: No stated basis for what made the planning or design good (structure, materials, timing) beyond general praise.
Timely relative to what event, need, or audience is left unspecified.

answer.phrase: enormous strength in continuous participatory change
answer.missing_criterion: No measure or mechanism given for how 'strength' is assessed or observed in this iterative process.

answer.phrase: Brilliant advice which might be hard for some egos to hear.
answer.missing_criterion: No criterion given for why the advice qualifies as 'brilliant' beyond the writer's approval.

answer.missing_context: Reads as a rebuttal to an unstated doubt about whether Rich and Nati genuinely have the experience being credited to them, but no such doubt or prior comment appears in the document.

answer.phrase: Simple, effective relationship building which is bound to reduce conflicts.
answer.missing_relationship: Asserts a causal link between the steward/stewardee pairing and reduced conflict without explaining the mechanism or offering evidence.

answer.phrase: If you can clearly define and agree which tool/s you will be using for each of these three essential areas of group work, your team is bound to be more effective.
answer.missing_relationship: Asserts a causal link between tool agreement and team effectiveness without specifying how or by what measure effectiveness follows.
